questions.q: Dry silver propanoate is refluxed with Br₂ in CCl₄. The organic product is:
questions.explain: The –COOAg group is replaced by Br and the carboxyl carbon leaves as CO₂, so the alkyl bromide has one carbon fewer. 2-Bromopropanoic acid would be the HVZ product, and butane the Kolbe-type dimer.

questions.q: The silver salt of an optically active acid whose stereocentre is the α-carbon undergoes the Hunsdiecker reaction. The alkyl bromide formed is:
options: Optically active with retention of configuration
Optically active with inversion of configuration
Racemic, because the reaction passes through a planar alkyl radical
questions.explain: After loss of CO₂ the alkyl radical is planar, so bromine bonds to either face equally. This loss of optical activity is classic evidence for the radical mechanism.

questions.q: Arrange the following by yield of alkyl bromide in the Hunsdiecker reaction of their silver salts: (I) CH₃CH₂CH₂COOAg, (II) (CH₃)₂CHCOOAg, (III) (CH₃)₃CCOOAg.
questions.explain: Yields fall in the order primary > secondary > tertiary for the alkyl group formed, so the straight-chain acid gives the best yield and the tertiary one the poorest. The trap is using carbocation stability (3° > 2° > 1°).

questions.q: The silver salt of a carboxylic acid RCOOAg is treated with iodine in a 2 : 1 molar ratio (salt : I₂). The main product is:
questions.explain: This is the Simonini reaction: a 1 : 1 ratio gives the alkyl iodide, but a 2 : 1 ratio gives mainly the ester RCOOR. That is why the Hunsdiecker method is used for chlorine and bromine.
